cards.text: Welcome to the proverbs of Solomon, king of Israel (Proverbs 1:1; 10:1). No plot twists here, friend, just short wise sayings packed one after another like cookies in a box. First up, Solomon sets a good name right next to great riches.

cards.question: Solomon says a good name is more desirable than great riches.

cards.text: And favor is better than silver and gold. Friend, Mother Miller bought me for a QUARTER, and I still wouldn't trade the name the Millers carved on my handle for a whole vault of the stuff.

cards.question: Solomon puts the rich and the poor side by side. What does he say they have in common?

answers.text: The LORD is Maker of them all
Toil is the lot of them all

cards.text: Next proverb: there's danger up ahead, and two kinds of people are walking toward it, the prudent and the simple.

cards.question: The prudent see the danger coming. What do they do?
Solomon says the simple come through the danger without a scratch.

cards.text: The simple keep going and suffer the consequences. That's me smelling smoke and telling the oven, "Two more minutes," then pulling out a batch I could've used to pave a DRIVEWAY.

cards.question: Solomon lists three rewards: wealth and honor and life. What two things bring them?

answers.text: Humility and the fear of the LORD
Sacrifice and the altar of the LORD
Courage and the favor of the king

cards.text: Then Solomon paints a path. On the path of the perverse lie thorns and snares, like my bakery floor at midnight after I knock over a whole jar of sprinkles.

cards.question: Thorns and snares lie on the path of the perverse. What does the one who guards his soul do?

cards.text: Next, Solomon talks about training a child in the way he should go. Friend, I told my six cookie cutter kids "press clean, lift straight" so many times, I started saying it in MY sleep.

cards.question: Solomon says a child trained in the way he should go will depart from it when he is old.

cards.text: Now money. Solomon says the rich rule over the poor, and then he tells us where the borrower stands.

cards.question: Solomon says the borrower is ___ to the lender.
Solomon switches to farming words. He who sows injustice will reap ___.

cards.text: Solomon adds that the rod of his fury will be destroyed. I once shook a rolling pin at a stubborn lump of dough so hard it snapped, and friend, the dough WON.
Next, Solomon says a generous man will be blessed, and he tells us exactly why. I'm generous too, friend, and every broken cookie in this bakery gets given away. Mostly to ME.

cards.question: Solomon says the generous man will be blessed. Why?

answers.text: He shares his bread with the poor
He gives fine gifts to the king
He lends money to his neighbors

cards.text: Then comes the mocker. Every group chat has one, and ONE comment from him turns a nice quiet morning into a three-hour argument.

cards.question: Solomon says drive out the mocker, and ___ will depart.

cards.text: Even quarreling and insults will cease. Then Solomon turns to someone who loves a pure heart and gracious lips.

cards.question: Solomon says the one who loves a pure heart and gracious lips will have the king for a friend.

cards.text: Now Solomon says the LORD's eyes keep watch over knowledge, and then he turns to the words of the faithless.

cards.question: Solomon says the LORD helps the words of the faithless come true.
The slacker won't leave the house, and he's got his reason all ready to go. What reason does he give?

answers.text: There are robbers on the road

cards.text: The slacker says, “There is a lion outside! I will be slain in the streets!” Friend, that's texting your boss, "Can't make it in today, there MIGHT be a dinosaur in the parking lot."
Then a serious warning. Solomon says the mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit.

cards.question: Solomon calls the mouth of an adulteress a deep pit. Who does he say will fall into it?

answers.text: He who is under the wrath of the LORD
He who is led astray by his friends
He who is wise in his own eyes

cards.text: Next, Solomon says foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child. Friend, I'm a grown stamper and I STILL open the oven every thirty seconds to see if the cookies are done yet.

cards.question: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child. What does Solomon say drives it far away?

cards.text: Last one, friend. Solomon names two things: oppressing the poor to enrich oneself, or giving gifts to the rich.

cards.question: Solomon names oppressing the needy to get rich, or giving gifts to the rich. He says either one will surely lead to ___.
